pr_title: fix(rust): Fix bug when casting to a local Categorical
pr_body:
When doing certain operations (e.g. first on an aggregation) we use the physicals in the categorical and later on cast them back. Casting from a `UInt32` to a `Categorical` now incorrectly assumes that the categorical is using the global string cache. Adjusted the cast to use the provided `rev_map` in the `dtype` which can either be global or local. 

This should be faster for global categoricals as there is no need to reconstruct the categories / mappings from the global cache (`from_global_indices`), however it does lead to slightly bigger maps / categoricals as they are not 'flattened' to the subset of values in the `UInt32Chunked`. There is a trade off here.

fix #11810
fix #11792
pr_comments:
I fixed the culprit. That was that `cast_unchecked` called `cast` while traversing nested types. That should be resolved as when we `cast_unchecked` we don't want to pay the price of bound checks/ rev-map construction etc.

Will post a PR.

issue_context.title: Panic on Displaying Series of List of List of Categorical
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://crates.io/crates/polars) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```rust
use polars::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    let categoricals = Series::new("categoricals", vec![Series::new("list", ["str"; 3]); 3])
        .cast(&DataType::List(Box::new(DataType::Categorical(None)))).unwrap();

    let categoricals = Series::new("categoricals", vec![categoricals; 3]);

    println!("{}", categoricals);
}
```


### Log output

```shell
shape: (3,)
Series: 'categoricals' [list[list[cat]]]
[
thread 'main' panicked at /Users/bytenybbler/Documents/Rust/Work/polars/crates/polars-core/src/chunked_array/ops/any_value.rs:56:22:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ComputeError(ErrString("cannot construct Categorical from these categories; at least one of them is out of bounds"))
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```


### Issue description

Displaying a Series that is a list[list[cat]] causes a panic. This panic also occurs when displaying any DataFrame that contains a column of type list[list[cat]].

### Expected behavior

Displaying a Series that is a list[list[cat]] should not cause a panic.

### Installed versions

<details>

polars = { version = "0.33.2", features = ["lazy", "dtype-categorical"] }

</details>
comments:
Calling `polars::enable_string_cache()` before printing the Series seems to prevent the panic.

This is because a Series cast occurs, turning `u32` into `cat`, and it attempts to call `CategoricalChunked::from_global_indices`. Without the string cache being enabled, the string cache is empty, and so the out-of-bounds check fails.

Interestingly, the panic doesn't happen when printing a Series of `list[cat]`. It just happens when printing something nested like `list[list[cat]]`.

I wonder how this should be fixed. I'd imagine it wouldn't be the user's responsibility to enable the string cache simply to print a nested list? Either way, the panic message is misleading and confusing.

This seems closely related to #11810.

review_comments:
We should only allow this in `cast_unchecked`. If we can with a rev-map that is not global we should probably panic here as that is an implementation error on our side.

I see that you check the bounds later, but I believe we can replace the `cast` with `cast_unchecked` on the proper locations to get the proper cast behavior without paying the bound check price.
